rule: §2 Types and values, re row: "`re` | `regexp` | No source regex uses lookaround or backreferences, so RE2 accepts them all. Compile at package level with regexp.MustCompile." The rule says nothing about character classes, so it implies the pattern text is copied as is.
row: none (the rows app/source.py L84 and L96 mention it only in passing as a "regex rule"; app/utils/emoji.py:9 and app/utils/text.py:7-8 have no row)
wrong_translation: Following the rule, an implementer writes regexp.MustCompile(`(#[\d\w]+)`) for source.py:24. Python 3 str patterns are Unicode-aware: \w matches any letter or digit (é, ü, Cyrillic, CJK), \d any Nd digit, \s any Unicode space. RE2's \w, \d and \s are ASCII only. For a post with "#café", Python makes the hashtag "#café" (href BASE_URL/t/café, tag name "#café", TaggedOutboxObject.tag "café"). Go makes "#caf" and leaves "é" as text. The Note's content and tag federate, and the stored tag changes what /t/{tag} lists. Mentions break the same way (source.py:25: @jürgen@example.com is not matched at all in Go, so there is no Mention tag and no cc). So do custom emoji names (emoji.py:9) and Article slugs (text.py:7 strips every non-ASCII letter).
proposed_fix: Amend §2 Types and values, re row, Notes: "Python 3 str patterns are Unicode-aware. RE2's \w, \d, \s and \b are ASCII only. Translate \w to [\p{L}\p{N}_], \d to \p{Nd}, and \s to Python's str.isspace set ([\t\n\v\f\r\x{1c}-\x{20}\x{85}\x{a0}\x{1680}\x{2000}-\x{200a}\x{2028}\x{2029}\x{202f}\x{205f}\x{3000}]), inside and outside brackets, with the negated forms as negated classes. Never copy a \w, \d or \s from a Python pattern unchanged. The inventory lists each pattern."

wrong_translation: verify_csrf_token declares csrf_token: str = Form(). FastAPI collects its "field required" error together with the route's own missing form fields and writes ONE 422 list, csrf_token first (probe: POST /admin/login with an empty form gives {"detail":[{"loc":["body","csrf_token"],...},{"loc":["body","password"],...}]}). A Go middleware that "only lets a request through or refuses it" either refuses with a 422 that lists only csrf_token, or lets the request through without a token. Neither gives the two-entry body. proposed_fix: Amend §2 HTTP, Middleware: "verify_csrf_token is not a pure middleware. When csrf_token is present, it verifies it and refuses with 403 at once. When csrf_token is missing or empty, it stores a pending 'field required' error for body.csrf_token in the request context and lets the request through. The next step that validates form fields (the session check for POST /admin/indieauth, then the route's own field validation) prepends that entry to its 422 list, or writes it alone when there is no other error."

rule: §2 Database, No identity map: "where the source reads a stale cached object, reproduce the stale read and mark it BUG(port):", and ADR 0017: "Where the original reads a stale cached object, as the outgoing worker does, the Go code reproduces the stale read with a BUG(port): marker, so the judge sees the original's behavior."
row: app/utils/workers.py Worker.run_forever (async with async_session() around the whole worker loop), SESSION_LONG_LIVED
wrong_translation: The row says: "Always reading current values is one of the original's own outcomes, so no BUG(port) marker." It contradicts the rule, which names this exact case. An implementer who follows the rule adds a per-worker cache of loaded objects and sends a poll as it was when first loaded. An implementer who follows the row reloads it. Example (mastodon__vote): after a vote, the outgoing worker sends a second delivery of the poll. With the rule, the Create keeps votersCount 0 and replies.totalItems 0. With the row, it carries votersCount 1. The judge's mastodon__vote scenario accepts both (internal/judge/scenarios_mastodon.go:63-80), so the row's choice is the cheaper one, but the rule and the ADR still tell implementers and reviewers to flag it.
proposed_fix: Amend §2 Database, No identity map, second bullet: "where the source reads a stale cached object only by chance (SQLAlchemy's identity map holds weak references, so the stale read depends on Python's garbage collector, as in the outgoing worker), read the current values and mark nothing; the inventory row says so. Where the stale read is certain (a strong reference held in the same function), reproduce it and mark it BUG(port):." Record it in an ADR that supersedes the outgoing-worker sentence of ADR 0017.

rule: §2 Database, Formats on disk, JSON: "0017 decides that the Go codec writes the same values, not the same bytes." ADR 0017: "The Go codec writes compact JSON with sorted keys and without HTML escaping."
wrong_translation: The row says "the database codec writes it as Python's json.dumps does". That contradicts the rule and the accepted ADR. Python stores {"items": [{"type": ["h-entry"], ...}], "rels": {...}} with ", " and ": " separators, insertion-order keys and \u-escaped non-ASCII text. The ADR's Go codec stores {"items":[{"properties":...,"type":["h-entry"]}],"rel-urls":...,"rels":...} with compact separators, sorted keys and raw UTF-8. An implementer or the codec's author who follows the row builds a second, Python-compatible encoder for this column only, so the column bytes differ from every other JSON column that the port writes.
proposed_fix: Row L145, replace "the database codec writes it as Python's json.dumps does" with "the database codec writes it (same values, not the same bytes: ADR 0017)".
